# pr-1627: gh-1625 [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

## PR Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

# pr-1627: gh-1625 [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1625` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +1147
- **Deletions**: -72
- **Created**: 2026-10-15T07:00:18Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-15T10:09:13Z

## PR Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

# pr-1627: gh-1625 [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

## PR Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

# pr-1627: gh-1625 [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

# warning, never to a skipped gate; the pre-check never reddens the run.
  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627, on a plain workflow_dispatch arm). The
      # check step itself is UNCONDITIONAL (no job-level if — a skipped
      # pre-check would empty its output), so the checkout must be too:
      # every arm that runs the step needs the file present. A shallow +
      # blobless fetch costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget — the
      # price of keeping the decision extracted to a script that the
      # static gate fixture-self-tests (the alternative, inlining like
      # release-pending, would orphan the selftested script; release-
      # pending stays checkout-free only because its logic IS inline).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twins
  # share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

## PR Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

# pr-1627: gh-1625 [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twins
  # share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

## PR Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

# pr-1627: gh-1625 [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]

# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#

EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0

      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then

    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

3578:  binaries:
---
  binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own GREEN push run IS
    # the gate (the dedupe lookup fires only on conclusion == "success") —
    # the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1627
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1627
- **Title**: gh-1625 [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1625` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 5
- **Additions**: +1147
- **Deletions**: -72
- **Created**: 2026-10-15T07:00:18Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-15T10:09:13Z

## PR Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

# pr-1627: gh-1625 [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

# warning, never to a skipped gate; the pre-check never reddens the run.
  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627, on a plain workflow_dispatch arm). The
      # check step itself is UNCONDITIONAL (no job-level if — a skipped
      # pre-check would empty its output), so the checkout must be too:
      # every arm that runs the step needs the file present. A shallow +
      # blobless fetch costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget — the
      # price of keeping the decision extracted to a script that the
      # static gate fixture-self-tests (the alternative, inlining like
      # release-pending, would orphan the selftested script; release-
      # pending stays checkout-free only because its logic IS inline).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twins
  # share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

---
  binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own GREEN push run IS
    # the gate (the dedupe lookup fires only on conclusion == "success") —
    # the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

## PR Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]

# pr-1627: gh-1625 [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

<details><summary>Graph behavior</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

</details>

    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on

    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would

      contents: read

      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twins
  # share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

---
  binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own GREEN push run IS
    # the gate (the dedupe lookup fires only on conclusion == "success") —
    # the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

# this job goes red — install.sh aborts with E_PROVENANCE_MISSING on it.
  # Needs web-spa (#1100, continue-on-error) for ordering only: the web
  # bundle cannot hold CLI provenance hostage. The ordering makes the fa-*
  # sweep deterministic — web-spa success -> zip signed, web-spa failure ->
  # zip absent — never a half-updated manifest.
  release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
---
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: bash scripts/pin_release.sh "${{ github.ref_name }}"

  installer-smoke:
    name: Installer smoke
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    needs: [binaries, release-provenance]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Depends on binaries — no !cancelled() needed here: the skip chain is
    # already broken upstream by the binaries job's own guard (fa#456).
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false

## PR Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).
- `release-dedupe` mirrors `release-pending` (`always() && startswith(refs/tags/)`); the gate chain becomes `pending == 'true' && dedupe != 'true'` across `quality-gate` and all 30 gate legs — mechanical, formulaic wiring, no per-job logic.
- `binaries` gains an explicit release arm (`always() && release`); `web-spa` stays keyed on `quality-gate.result == 'success'` so it skips on the deduped twin (binaries-attach only).
- Push / workflow_dispatch / schedule arms untouched; concurrency rule (never cancel tag runs) untouched.
- Regression guard follows the `aab-gate-selftest` pattern: the static test `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` (stubbed `gh API`) plus `dart test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart`; a live dependency-graph simulation replayed the real `needs`/`if` semantics for AC1/AC2/AC3.

### How to verify

```bash
bash scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh
dart test test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart test/ci_release_pending_guard_test.dart
dart test   # full suite: +10984 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed
```

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  TAG[push: v* tag] --> RP[release-pending]
  RP --> RD[release-dedupe]
  RD -->|dedupe=false| GATE[full quality gate]
  RD -->|dedupe=true| ATT[binaries + provenance + installer-smoke only]
```

# pr-1627: gh-1625 [INFRA] ci.yml double-fires the full quality gate on release tags (push v* + release published) — dedupe the release-event run to binaries-only

## Description

Closes #1625
## What changed

Release tags no longer double-fire the full quality gate: a new `release-dedupe` pre-check job short-circuits the tag twin's gate when a completed `push` CI run for the same tag already exists — while the release-specific legs (binaries-attach, provenance, installer smoke) keep running on it.

### Key decisions

- Extracted the dedupe decision into `scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` (default **dedupe=false**, flips only on a successful lookup of a push run for the same tag ref/workflow/any status) — fails safe, preserving the old-tag safety net (AC2).

  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it

    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627, on a plain workflow_dispatch arm). The
      # check step itself is UNCONDITIONAL (no job-level if — a skipped
      # pre-check would empty its output), so the checkout must be too:
      # every arm that runs the step needs the file present. A shallow +
      # blobless fetch costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget — the
      # price of keeping the decision extracted to a script that the
      # static gate fixture-self-tests (the alternative, inlining like
      # release-pending, would orphan the selftested script; release-
      # pending stays checkout-free only because its logic IS inline).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]

    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'

# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twins
  # share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"
